validity.recommendation: Do not 'fix' LengthKnownKm to the measured 429 km schematic draw — per protocol gotcha 3 a drawn span exceeding the stated value only counts as evidence when it FAR exceeds it (this brief's own P0776 sibling row is the sharper case of that; P0775's ratio of 1.44 is milder). Instead flag LengthKnownKm=298.00 as likely SCOPE-PARTIAL rather than simply wrong: it most plausibly measures the shared Yelets-Kursk trunk segment common to both this line and P0776, not the full Yelets-to-Dykanka corridor the row's own PipelineName promises. A human should treat 298.00 as low-confidence-scope and look specifically for a Ukrtransgaz/Ukrtransgaz-successor asset-register entry for the 'Kursk-Dykanka' leg (utg.ua and tsoua.com both 403 live per gotcha 1 — retry via Wayback with a later/different snapshot than the one I used, which covers the corporate chronology page, not an asset register) before recording any corrected value. Do not touch StartYear1 (1984) — the Ukrtransgaz chronology corroborates it exactly and it is not part of this brief's flag.
validity.researcher_notes: This brief's only flagged question for P0775 is length_ratio (429 km drawn vs 298.00 km stated); the redundancy leg's existence/duplicate verdict and the staged Gazprom-ownership-attribution concern are both already settled elsewhere and I have not re-litigated them. Findings, worked as one problem with the sibling row P0776 per the brief's instruction (both rows share the corridor and the 189.3 km Yelets-Kursk geodesic prefix measured in Leg 2): (1) Ukrtransgaz's own official corporate chronology (utg.ua, reached via Wayback because the live site 403s per gotcha 1) confirms this pipeline's 1984 commissioning as its own single, one-time build: '1984 р. Введено в експлуатацію магістральний газопровід Єлець - Курськ – Диканька' ('In 1984, the Yelets-Kursk-Dykanka trunk gas pipeline was commissioned') — no staged/later-extension entry exists for this line the way there is for P0776's corridor (see that row's shard), so I cannot invoke the same two-stage-build argument here; this line really was completed as one project. (2) Gazprom Transgaz Moskva's own 'Yelets LPUMG' branch page (moskva-tr.gazprom.ru, via Wayback — the live URL failed to connect for me too, matching the source_ladder's note) confirms the physical reality of a single continuous line from the Yelets hub to Dykanka via Kursk, naming it directly: 'через КС Єлець проходять два газопроводи «Петровськ-Єлець», далі «Елец-Курск-Киев»... і «Петровськ-Єлець» (розширення), далі «Елец-Курск-Диканька», що забезпечують природним газом Україну' — but gives no length figure for either leg. (3) Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated article on this line lists four compressor stations along its route (Yelets, Kursk, Cheremisinovo, and Sumy — commissioned 1985, per the article, the year AFTER this line's own 1984 completion date, which is itself a small inconsistency in that source I am not resolving here since it isn't my flag), spanning Lipetsk, Kursk, and Sumy oblasts before reaching Poltava oblast (Dykanka) — a corridor of that geographic extent is very difficult to reconcile with a total pipe length of only 298 km when the shared Yelets-Kursk prefix alone geodesics at 189.3 km. (4) I could not find any source stating a full corridor length in km for this line. Searched and struck out: energybase.ru (cited on gem.wiki for this row) IP-blocks this research environment and is robots-excluded from Wayback (confirmed via the CDX 'excluded from the Wayback Machine' notice), so I could not check it as GEM's possible length origin. Kursk Oblast's and Lipetsk Oblast's official 'gas supply system characteristics' documents (e-gorod.ru, dated to 01.01.2001, reached via Wayback) each give only oblast-wide aggregate trunk-pipeline mileage (Kursk: 1,512.5 km total across all 6 named trunk lines crossing the oblast; Lipetsk: 2,299.5 km across 14 named lines) plus per-compressor-station equipment tables — never a per-pipeline length breakdown, so neither document isolates this line's own length. Conclusion: given P0775 and P0776 carry near-identical stated lengths (298.00 vs 297.00) despite P0776 being independently documented (see that shard) as a two-stage build whose SECOND stage alone materially lengthens its corridor beyond Kursk, the most coherent reading is that both cells measure the same shared Yelets-Kursk segment, not either line's full nominal corridor. This is inferential for P0775 specifically (I have no equivalent staged-build documentation for the Dykanka leg the way I do for the Kyiv leg) but is the reading most consistent with all sources found. A true full-corridor length for the Dykanka leg remains unresolved.
